data_flow:
The section will trace the end-to-end Phase 4 planner loop data flow as built:
1. Scope capture (T1): A caller posts `scope.captured` to `POST /rooms/:roomId/events` with a `goal` string. `prepareFounderGoal` checks bounds and credential patterns, attaches `{ kind: 'founder_goal', ref: event.eventId, digest }` to `evidence`, and stores `goal` in the room event payload.
2. Round opening and journal-before-dispatch (T2): `PlannerLoop.runRound` reads the room state under the fenced leader store. In `SCOPED`, it computes `plannerCommandIdFor(roomId, openingEventId, 1)`, in one Postgres transaction appends T2 `task.dispatched.planner` and writes the command's `journaled` row (`appendJournaled`), and checks the route via its `authorizeRoute` dependency (which `counted-run.ts` supplies).
3. Gateway poll, attestation, and execution: `GatewayPlannerWorker` polls `POST /gateway/planner/poll`. On `attest`, it queries `executor.attest`; `PlannerLoop` verifies `role === 'architect'` and the intended route and writes `identity_bound`. On `execute`, `PlannerRecordStore` writes a durable `starting` record (its phases are `attested`, `starting`, `not_sent`, `running`, `finished`, and `lost`; `accepted` is the answer to `execute`) before `AgyPlannerExecutor` verifies the root-owned `agy` binary SHA-256, prepares a read-only checkout of the whole repository at `baseSha` (the scope paths go only into the prompt), spawns `agy` with `PINNED_AGY_ARGUMENTS`, waits for the first stream-json `init` line confirming `init.model === 'gemini-4-argon-high'` before writing the prompt to stdin, and extracts the `plandoc/1` JSON object.
4. Init verification, plan judgment, and atomic T3 commit: `PlannerLoop` requires `PlannerInit` for `antigravity` + `google`, writes `dispatched` carrying `init_model` and `provider_conversation_id`, and checks observed vs intended route. When `awaitPlan` returns the raw document, `judgeRoundPlan` runs `judgePlanDoc` and checks `repository`, `base_sha`, and `scope_paths` against the captured scope. `submitRoundPlan` then commits T3 `plan.submitted` (with `plandoc` evidence carrying `planHash`), `PlanStore.recordPlan`, and the journal `completed` row in one transaction.
5. Plan read, Founder decision (T4/T5/T22), and revision: The Founder reads the plan via `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan` and posts `plan.revision_requested`, `plan.approved`, or `founder.cancel` to `POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision`, which commits the lifecycle event and `decision` journal row (`JournalTransaction.appendDecision`) in one transaction. On T4, the next `PlannerLoop.runRound` in `PLANNING` loads the prior plan from `PlanStore`, verifies its `planHash` against T4's `revisingPlanHash`, and passes `earlierPlan` and `feedback` into the revision round.
trust_and_security_boundaries:
The `README.md` section will document the security boundaries enforced in code:
1. Runtime database role and append-only tables: `JournalStore` and `PlanStore` run as `br_app_runtime`. `public.build_room_plans` (`0010_plan_store`) forbids `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, and `TRUNCATE` and grants only `SELECT, INSERT` to `br_app_runtime`.
2. Governed event path enforcement: `POST /rooms/:roomId/events` rejects `GOVERNED_PATH_EVENTS` with `403 governed_path_required` (`packages/control-plane/src/server.ts` lines 236-239), preventing callers from forging server-derived guard facts or bypassing journal writes.
3. Token separation: `CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN` guards room events and `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan`; `PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN` exclusively guards `POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision`; `PHASE4_COUNTED_RUN_TOKEN` exclusively guards `/control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round` and `/control-plane/rooms/:roomId/journal`, and must differ from both `CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN` and `PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN` (`packages/control-plane/src/config.ts` lines 321-334).
4. Pre-write redaction and value-redacted refusals: `prepareFounderGoal`, `PlanStore.recordPlan`, `plan-decision.ts`, and `JournalStore` reject credential material via `containsCredentialMaterial`. When a planner output fails validation, `PlannerLoop` logs `planner.plan_refused` with value-redacted `PlanRefusalReason` diagnostics and never stores the refused body.
5. Isolated Linux planner execution: `AgyPlannerExecutor` runs only on Linux Gateway `1880c12d-d98d-4a91-b25a-23320aa7f58a`, verifies the root-owned `agy` binary SHA-256 before execution, withholds the prompt until `init.model === 'gemini-4-argon-high'` is observed, runs `agy` in `--mode plan --sandbox`, reaps processes with `pkill -KILL -u <plannerUser>`, and writes `planner-halted.json` on any cleanup or probe failure.

error_and_failure_behavior:
The `README.md` section will summarize the fail-closed behaviors built into the Phase 4 planner loop:
1. Unfenced or non-leader control plane: `PlannerLoop` throws `PlannerLoopUnfencedError` if constructed without a fenced store; `POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision` and `POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round` run behind `requireLeader` (`packages/control-plane/src/server.ts` lines 362 and 394).
2. Pre-contact vs post-contact failures and retry budget: Only an affirmative `not_sent` transport failure may be retried within `DISPATCH_POLICY.transport_retries_max` (up to `MAX_ROUND_ATTEMPTS = 3`), and only when `retryBudgetTransition` allows (`packages/control-plane/src/planner-loop.ts` lines 558-568). A route mismatch and a refused plan are recorded `failed` (`route_mismatch`, `plan_invalid`, `plan_outside_captured_scope`), while dispatch or wait errors and an agy-lane acceptance without the init fields are recorded `unresolved`, with no automatic retry.
3. Gateway at-most-one discipline and executor halt: `PlannerRecordStore` writes no `accepted` record; its phases are `attested`, `starting`, `not_sent`, `running`, `finished`, and `lost` (`accepted` is the answer to `execute`), and `not_sent` and `never_received` are answered only when the executor's own `sent` record says `false`. If `AgyPlannerExecutor` cannot confirm a clean process table or workspace cleanup, it writes `planner-halted.json` and refuses subsequent runs until cleared.
4. Recovery (called only by tests; no production code calls `PlannerRecovery`): `PlannerRecovery.recoverRoom` runs `journal.verify()` from genesis first; for an open command it queries `planner.reconcile(commandId)`, writing `failed` (`not_sent`) on `never_received` before dispatch, judging and submitting T3 or recording `failed` when `finished`, or recording `unresolved` when ambiguous or mismatched.
5. Counted-run harness fail-closed gates: `Phase4Runner` does not need an existing `attempts.json` (without one `attempt-store.ts` starts an empty log); `phase4:counted-run` acquires an exclusive `run.lock`, runs `evaluatePhase4Entry` before any room is created, runs `evaluatePhase4LiveCheck`, executes one label per invocation, and records outcomes `not_started`, `passed`, `failed`, `interrupted`, and `rejected`, writing `<label>-<roomId>.record.json` when a run produces a record.
observability:
The `README.md` section will document the observability and audit surfaces built for Phase 4:
1. Hash-chained command journal (`public.command_journal`): records `journaled`, `identity_bound`, `dispatched` (carrying `init_model` and `provider_conversation_id`), `completed`, `failed`, `unresolved`, and `decision` rows (`plan.approved`, `plan.revision_requested`, `founder.cancel`), reconstructable via `reconstruct()` and inspectable via `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/journal` during a counted run.
2. Durable plan store (`public.build_room_plans`): stores the canonical `plandoc/1` JSON and `plan_hash` keyed by `command_id` and `(room_id, lifecycle_event_id)`, readable via `GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan`.
3. Structured planner refusal logging: logs `planner.plan_refused` with `roomId`, `commandId`, `classification`, and `reason` (which has a `kind` and, for a schema failure, `violationCount` and `violations` with `code` and `path`).
4. Gateway and harness local artifacts: `PlannerRecordStore` (`<gatewayDirectory>/planner/<sha256(commandId)>.json`), `AgyPlannerExecutor` per-command evidence (`<gatewayDirectory>/planner-evidence/<sha256(commandId)>.json` and `planner-halted.json`), and Phase 4 harness records (`attempts.json`, `plan-<planHash>.json`, and `<label>-<roomId>.record.json`).
